title: DWG class string-footer unaligned bit offsets fast slice
mode: Generated in-memory regression plus bounded local corpus check

researchBasis.source: Open Design Specification for .dwg files v5.4.1
researchBasis.formatRule: R2007+ string-stream size words are located relative to an end bit; the low word high bit indicates an additional high-size word.
researchBasis.authority: ODA v5.4.1 is normative for DWG byte layout.

cases: Existing byte-aligned high-bit extension control retained.
Generated high-size/flagged-low-size/footer-bit cases at each bit offset 1 through 7.
Each case asserts decoded string size, start bit, and returned buffer cursor.

localCorpusAudit.readObservations: All nine detailed traces observed operationSucceeded=true and legacyError=0; one reported a classes CRC warning, and several reported incomplete frame coverage.
localCorpusAudit.cliFailureBoundary: Strict DXF export preflight required a successful complete DWG read disposition; this is separate from a classes-footer parse failure.
localCorpusAudit.assessment: The known AC1024 RTM error-8 report was not reproduced by these available files; they do not resolve it without the exact failing inputs and are not support/acceptance evidence.

limitations: The generated bit-offset vectors exercise the shared size-footer helper, not complete DWG class sections from an independent producer.
The local AC1024 corpus smoke did not include the exact reported failing RTM saves; the known class-parser issue remains unresolved.
Strict conversion failures and partial frame observations are not evidence of successful output or general DWG support.
The shared worktree is broadly dirty and repository Git metadata is read-only; this slice is uncommitted.
nextReadinessSlice: Continue with the next local source/spec-backed PAR-07/PAR-14 implementation item; keep the known AC1024 RTM class failure open until an exact failing save is available.
